subject: GroundTruth Health — capacity framing & SLA options
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@groundtruth.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-16T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: GroundTruth Health — capacity framing & SLA options

Hi Elena — thanks again for the intro call today. Quick recap while it's fresh and a proposed next-step plan.

Key pain points you called out:
- Production latency inconsistencies at 95th percentile (esp. for clinical triage flows) causing user friction.
- Regulatory constraints (HIPAA, auditability) requiring tenant isolation and longer log retention.
- Need predictable cost for planning: current cloud spend spikes when batch workloads run overnight.

Goals we heard you on:
1) Isolated GPU pools for PHI workloads with per-tenant encryption at rest.
2) <50 ms median token latency for short chat paths, 200 ms P95 target for the majority of inference.
3) A procurement-friendly pricing band (monthly committed + measured burst).

Initial capacity framing (ballpark):
- Committed pool: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs (resident) to cover steady-state inference.
- Burst window: scalable up to 12 GPUs for nightly batch/retrospective scoring.
- Ops SLAs: 99.9% uptime for the pool, targeted P95 latency guardrails tied to model variants and batching settings.

Immediate next steps I propose:
1) Technical deep-dive with Marissa (solutions) and Ben (ops) — target: 60-minute call next week to map real traffic patterns and sequence-length distribution.
2) Ben will draft operational SLO options and a pricing sketch (committed + burst) for your procurement team.
3) You to share the SLA asks spreadsheet you mentioned (we can annotate).

I'll attach a short template for SLA asks and a placeholder network diagram so we can iterate. Happy to shift timelines if your procurement window is tighter.

Thanks — Jonas
Jonas Weber

Thanks Jonas — that's a helpful summary and aligns with our notes. Couple clarifications: 

- The 50 ms median is for our conversational clinical assistant (short prompts, <= 128 tokens). For the batch scoring (full patient history), latency is less critical but throughput and deterministic completion during nightly windows matter a lot.
- Isolation must be verifiable: we need audit logs and separate KMS scopes per environment (staging vs prod).
- Procurement timeline: we'd like a commercial proposal by June 2 to brief legal the week after (tight timeline).

I've attached the SLA asks template you mentioned and added two rows with priorities from legal (retention periods and incident notification windows).

Elena

Elena — copying technical notes from our pre-call so we have a concrete checklist for the deep-dive. I also sketched an ops playbook and a few config knobs we'll likely recommend.

Short technical summary / assumptions:
- Model mix: 70% short-chat seq (<=128 tokens), 30% long-context scoring (>=1024 tokens) for nightly jobs.
- Preferred model variants: quantized for batch scoring; FP16 (or BF16) resident variants for low-latency chat.
- KV cache persistence: use in-memory for chat (to keep latency low) + prefix cache for common prompts.

Recommended configuration to meet your targets:
1) Dedicated pool of 4x A100-eq GPUs pinned to prod tenant; autoscale policy for short bursts (scale step: +2 GPUs, cooldown 90s).
2) Separate batch worker cluster with pre-warmed quantized models for nightly scoring (job window 0200-0600 PT).
3) Network & security: VPC peering + customer-managed KMS (we support BYOK/HSM); audit log retention configurable up to 7 years.
4) Observability: per-route P95 dashboards, token-level cost breakdown, and alerting for latency increases >20% baseline.

Open questions for the call:
- Can you share a 2-week sample of traffic (timestamps, seq lengths, qps) and a redacted example prompt distribution? That will let us size the burst policy more precisely.
- Any hard constraints on daytime cost budgeting vs batch windows?

I've attached the network diagram Jonas referenced and a short ops playbook draft (in the Drive link Jonas included). Will prep a slide with SLO options and cost deltas for the June 2 commercial draft.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Marissa / Jonas — quick note from the procurement side. Two constraints to flag: 
1) We need a month-to-month POC option (no long-term commit) to start — legal will not sign an annual commit before we validate latency and audit controls. The POC can include a capped committed baseline and a defined burst credit.
2) Budget window: Q3 budget is already allocated; any commercial offer will need to be structured as a 3-month pilot expense in Q2 for validation.

If Redwood can provide a POC contract with a clear exit and an evaluation checklist (SLOs to verify), we can greenlight a technical POC immediately after the deep-dive.

Thanks — Chris
Chris Liu
Head of Procurement, GroundTruth Health
chris.liu@groundtruth.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-05-18T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: GroundTruth Health — capacity framing & SLA options

Elena / Chris — thanks for the clarity. Action items and owners below (I'll own the commercial sketch + POC contract language):

1) Marissa: run the technical deep-dive with GroundTruth engineers (request: two 60-minute slots Wed/Thu next week).
2) Jonas: collect the 2-week traffic sample and the SLA asks spreadsheet with priorities annotated (Elena — can you share the redacted traffic dump to jonas.weber@redwood.ai?).
3) Ben: draft POC contract (month-to-month, capped commit with burst credits) + commercial table for June 2 delivery.
4) Security: we'll include an operations annex covering KMS, audit logs, and evidence points for HIPAA readiness.

Preliminary commercial approach (high level):
- Pilot (90 days): 2x committed GPUs + burst pool up to 6 GPUs; pilot credits applied for first month to de-risk validation.
- Post-Pilot: convert to monthly reserved pool (scale to 4 committed GPUs) or annual committed discounted path depending on uptake.

Timeline: aiming to have the commercial draft and POC language to you by 2027-06-02 for legal review. If we need to accelerate, let us know and we'll prioritize.

I'll attach an internal checklist afterward and follow up with a calendar invite for the deep-dive.

—Ben
